raw_case_text:
The reported patient is a 67-year-old female who resides in the southwestern United States with notable past medical history of asthma and asbestosis. Notably, there was no history of immunosuppression nor infectious diseases prior to the present episode. She underwent resection of a 11.2 x 7.5 cm well-differentiated liposarcoma of the abdominal wall in July 2018. At the time of initial evaluation at our center in February 2019, she was noted to have a 4.6 x 4.7 cm recurrent vs. residual focus of disease between the left internal oblique and left transversus abdominus muscles for which the patient remains in observation (Figure 1).
The patient has given informed consent for publication of this case.
In June 2020, the patient developed shortness of breath, increased fatigue and cough. No fever was documented or reported. An initial COVID-19 polymerase chain reaction test was obtained by the patient's local physician and was positive. No further laboratory or imaging evaluation was obtained at that time point. Multiple subsequent COVID-19 tests were negative, however, the patient's symptoms persisted.
A bronchoscopy was performed in July 2020 and the patient was diagnosed with an atypical mycobacterial infection (mycobacterium avium intracellulare) for which antibiotics were not recommended. At that time, the coccidioides serology was indeterminate for IgM, negative for IgG and antibody titers were negative.
In September 2020, symptoms persisted and computed tomography (CT) imaging revealed subcentimeter pulmonary nodules and small sclerotic bony lesions. As the lesions were too small to biopsy, close interval follow-up was recommended.
In November 2020, the patient palpated a new right chest wall mass. She reported pulmonary symptomatic improvement of prior respiratory symptoms and was without fever or systemic inflammatory symptoms. Follow-up CT imaging demonstrated new bilateral pulmonary nodules, a 4.8 x 2.7 cm right anterior chest mass extending from the pectoralis major muscle into the costochondral junction of the right third rib, areas of sclerotic foci in axial bones and a slow progression of the known left abdominal wall recurrent vs. residual liposarcoma measuring 5.5 x 5.1 cm (Figures 2A,C,E).
The appearance of new lung nodules, bone lesions and chest wall mass in this patient with liposarcoma was suspicious for distant metastatic lesions. The patient thus presented to our institution in advance of her usual surveillance visit for further evaluation. Although the radiographic features of these lesions were consistent with metastatic disease, well-differentiated liposarcomas are only rarely known to distantly metastasize. A biopsy was therefore recommended to confirm the diagnosis of metastatic liposarcoma prior to initiation of chemotherapy.
In December 2020, a core needle biopsy of the right chest wall mass was performed. The patient developed a right chest wall cellulitis post-biopsy which was treated and resolved with Doxycycline. The pathological examination found no evidence of malignant cells but revealed granulomatous inflammation with necrosis and rare spherical structures highlighted by Grocott's Methenamine Silver stain suggestive of fungal organisms (Figures 3A,B).
White blood cell count displayed a lymphopenia with a lymphocyte count of 430/mm3. Serology and antigen for cryptococcus were negative, as was the intra-dermal tuberculosis test.
Serological tests for coccidioidomycosis were negative for IgM and positive for IgG. Coccidioidomycosis complement fixation (CF) titer was 1:32.
Systemic anti-fungal treatment with oral fluconazole 400 mg daily was initiated with close follow-up and imaging. Patient remains under treatment with good tolerance. No other therapeutic intervention has been required.
In April 2021, patient reported persistent asthenia and shortness of breath but no cough. CT imaging showed decrease in lung nodules and chest wall mass which now measured 3.2 x 1.3 cm (Figures 2D,F). The sclerotic bony lesions were unchanged (Figure 2B). The residual abdominal wall liposarcoma was stable in size comparison to December 2020, with slight increase compared to postoperative imaging in February 2019. CF titer was 1:16. Lymphocyte count was 740/mm3.
The patient continues fluconazole treatment for an additional 6 months before repeat imaging and clinical follow-up.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 67-year-old female with a history of resected abdominal wall well-differentiated liposarcoma presented with a newly palpated right anterior chest wall mass following 5 months of persistent dyspnea, fatigue, and cough.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In June 2020, the patient (under surveillance for a 4.6 x 4.7 cm recurrent/residual left abdominal wall well-differentiated liposarcoma) developed dyspnea, fatigue, and cough with an initial positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR. Her respiratory symptoms persisted despite negative repeat COVID-19 tests, with July 2020 bronchoscopy isolating Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare (untreated) and September 2020 CT showing subcentimeter lung nodules and small sclerotic bone lesions. In November 2020, she palpated a new right anterior chest wall mass while her prior cough had improved.
subjective.past_medical_history: Well-differentiated abdominal wall liposarcoma (11.2 x 7.5 cm resected July 2018; residual/recurrent 4.6 x 4.7 cm focus observed since Feb 2019), asthma, asbestosis, prior COVID-19 (June 2020), and pulmonary Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare colonization (July 2020); resident of the southwestern United States; no prior immunosuppression.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for right anterior chest wall mass, persistent asthenia, and shortness of breath. Negative for fever or systemic inflammatory symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: Palpable right anterior chest wall mass; developed post-biopsy right chest wall cellulitis that resolved with oral doxycycline.
objective.routine_investigations: Lymphopenia with lymphocyte count 430/mm3 (improving to 740/mm3 in April 2021). Cryptococcus antigen and serology and intradermal tuberculin test were negative. Coccidioides serology (previously indeterminate IgM and negative IgG in July 2020) converted to positive IgG with a complement fixation (CF) titer of 1:32 (declining to 1:16 in April 2021).
objective.advanced_workup: November 2020 CT demonstrated new bilateral pulmonary nodules, a 4.8 x 2.7 cm right anterior chest wall mass extending from the pectoralis major into the right third rib costochondral junction, axial skeletal sclerotic lesions, and slow growth of the left abdominal wall liposarcoma (5.5 x 5.1 cm). Core needle biopsy of the right chest wall mass showed no malignancy but revealed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with rare spherical fungal organisms highlighted by Grocott's methenamine silver (GMS) stain.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis of disseminated coccidioidomycosis (involving the lungs, axial skeleton, and right anterior chest wall/third rib) mimicking metastatic liposarcoma following COVID-19, confirmed by right chest wall core biopsy histopathology (necrotizing granulomas with GMS-positive spherules), positive Coccidioides IgG, and complement fixation titer of 1:32; metastatic liposarcoma, tuberculosis, and cryptococcosis were excluded. Treated with oral fluconazole 400 mg daily (planned for at least 10+ months), resulting in regression of the pulmonary nodules, reduction of the chest wall mass to 3.2 x 1.3 cm, and decline of the CF titer to 1:16 at 4-month follow-up.
